name: Pairs of Numbers
description: Let's assume that we have a pair of numbers ( a , b ). We can get a new pair ( a + b , b ) or ( a , a + b ) from the given pair in a single step. Let the initial pair of numbers be (1,1). Your task is to find number k , that is, the least number of steps needed to transform (1,1) into the pair where at least one number equals n .
input_specification: The input contains the only integer n ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 6 ).
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 134B — Pairs of Numbers [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
